CanonicalStatus.description:
How the page's identity URL was chosen.

``self``          declared canonical equals the page's own URL
``declared``      a different, in-scope canonical was declared and is used
``missing``       none declared; the normalised final URL is used
``out_of_scope``  declared canonical is off-site; ignored, final URL used
``invalid``       declared canonical is unparseable; ignored, final URL used

Precedence at persistence (prevents identity flip-flop): a ``self`` or
``missing`` document is the AUTHORITY for its identity URL. A ``declared``
(alias) document may create identity X only while X has no version from an
authoritative document; once it has, the alias records ``known_urls`` Y -> X
plus a ``duplicate_canonical`` issue and writes no version. Within one run,
the authoritative document for X always wins over aliases of X.
CanonicalStatus.title: CanonicalStatus

EventName.description:
The TRD.md section 15 vocabulary, plus governed additions.

Phase 0 emits only ``worker.heartbeat``. The remaining names are frozen
here so later phases cannot invent divergent spellings for the same fact.

Additions beyond TRD.md section 15, each an explicit decision:

* ``skill.promoted`` -- added at the user's direction (post-Phase-0
  cleanup, 2026-10-13). TRD.md had ``policy.promoted`` but no skill
  equivalent, although AUTONOMY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md makes PROMOTE_SKILL an
  ASK-level action, which therefore needs an audit event.
* ``worker.heartbeat`` -- operational, recorded in docs/adr/ADR-0005.md.
* ``job.completed`` -- operational, Phase 2 (docs/adr/ADR-0010-content-intelligence.md):
  every finished generic job run (analysis, recommendation, verification,
  analytics import, evaluation, autonomy shadow), including failed ones.
  Ingestion keeps ``crawl.completed``.

Governed lifecycles (no learning behaviour is implemented yet)::

    skill.proposed  -> offline/human evaluation -> skill.promoted
    policy.proposed -> offline/human evaluation -> policy.promoted

Proposal is ALLOW for agents; promotion is ASK and requires a human. Both
``*.promoted`` events must carry a :class:`PromotionAuditPayload`, which
:class:`EventEnvelope` enforces.

ExperimentKind.description:
What an experiment varies. Both kinds exist; ``holdout`` is DEFAULTED OFF, not omitted.

ADR-0016 16.4 cut ``holdout`` entirely; the user has since decided it is built and gated
instead. Withholding links from live pages is a real editorial and SEO cost, so the safety
is three independent gates rather than a missing enum member:

1. ``treatment_fraction <= 0.20`` for a ``holdout`` -- a hard maximum, CHECKed in the
   database as well as here. The policy default is
   :data:`DEFAULT_HOLDOUT_TREATMENT_FRACTION` (0.10).
2. ``Settings.experiments_allow_holdout`` defaults ``False``, and
   ``ExperimentLifecycle.activate`` refuses ``draft -> active`` for a ``holdout`` with
   :attr:`ExperimentRefusal.HOLDOUT_NOT_ENABLED` while it is unset.
3. The same transaction must hold the transaction-local
   :data:`EXPERIMENT_ACTIVATOR_SETTING`, which only that one service sets -- so a raw
   ``UPDATE experiments SET status = 'active'`` cannot start a holdout either.
ExperimentKind.title: ExperimentKind

ExperimentUnit.description:
Which page an arm is assigned to -- determined by the kind, never chosen freely.

This resolves the arm-contamination bug the pre-fan-out review found (ADR-0016 15.5): the
draft assigned arms by SOURCE page while saying a holdout's comparison is the TARGET page's
metric. Those are different pages, so the arms were contaminated -- nothing stopped a
control page from receiving inbound links from an unassigned source.

Resolution (a) of the two the user offered: **a holdout assigns by TARGET page**, and
``locked()`` refuses any plan whose TARGET is a control page. That is coherent with the
existing ``ExperimentGuard.locked(*, source_page_id, target_page_id)`` signature, which
already takes both pages, and it is the question a holdout is actually for -- "withhold
inbound links from these pages and compare their search performance".
ExperimentUnit.title: ExperimentUnit

LinkPlanStatus.description:
PRD v1.1 Appendix C recommendation lifecycle. Moves only along ``ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS``.

ADR-0018 adds ``autonomy_decided`` and ``blocked`` and makes the approval pair
EXCEPTIONAL. The normal autonomous path is::

    proposed -> critiqued -> policy_checked -> autonomy_decided -> validated
             -> deployed -> verified -> measured -> learning_captured

``awaiting_approval`` / ``approved`` stay reachable, but only for an operator acting on an
exception. They are no longer on the normal path (ADR-0018 s3). A ``guarded``-mode DEFERRAL
is NOT recorded as ``awaiting_approval``: it is ``blocked`` with an empty block list (the
database guard maps every ``block`` decision to ``blocked``; ADR-0018 "Corrections after
integration" item 1), and an operator can still publish-override it.

``unresolved``      never led to a page: beyond crawl limits, robots-blocked or errored
``not_applicable``  the link is not internal

PlacementLocator.description:

only behind ``read_settings``.

they are never rendered as code and never interpolated into SQL.

``target_paths`` holds EVERY file a promotion would write. For ``ranking`` that is TWO

``policies/recommendation/recommendation.v1.yaml``'s ``ranking_policy:`` pointer by
``resolve_ranking_policy``, NOT from ``Settings`` -- so promoting weights also requires a
new recommendation document. Only the CLI writes a policy file; the API records the event.

ReadinessResponse.description:
``GET /ready`` -- aggregate readiness.

HTTP status mapping, implemented in the router and asserted by tests:

==================  =====  ===============================
aggregate status    code   headers
==================  =====  ===============================
ready               200    Cache-Control: no-store
degraded            200    Cache-Control: no-store
not_ready           503    no-store, Retry-After: 5
==================  =====  ===============================

A probe that itself raises yields 503 with that check marked ERROR -- never
a 500, because an unhandled exception in a readiness probe is still a
readiness answer.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

ReadinessStatus.description:
Aggregate verdict over all dependency checks.

The distinction between DEGRADED and NOT_READY is the whole point of the
``required`` flag on each check: an optional dependency that is missing
degrades the service without making it unready. Qdrant and Ollama are both
optional by default, so their absence must not take the API down.
ReadinessStatus.title: ReadinessStatus
